title: Sheaf.H acyclicity of an injective ModuleCat-valued sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring, and let $J$ be an injective object of the category of ModuleCat-valued sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Its underlying abelian sheaf $J_{ab}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] has $H^q(X,J_{ab})=0$ for $q>0$, where cohomology is Sheaf.H [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No torsion assumption, affine hypothesis, or closed immersion occurs. In Lean the coefficient ring may have universe u+1 while X has universe u.

source.place: Lemma cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, second paragraph of proof, applied to the terminal object of the small etale site

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-constant-ring-equivalence to identify ModuleCat-valued sheaves with modules over the constant ring sheaf, retaining underlying abelian sheaves by its natural forgetful-functor isomorphism. The equivalence preserves injectivity. The free module Cech complex of every covering is exact in positive homological degrees.

The underlying presheaf of modules of an injective sheaf of modules is injective. Apply the exact functor Hom(-,J) to the free complex; by Yoneda the resulting complex is the Cech complex. Its positive cohomology vanishes. Forgetting coefficients retains this complex.

The Cech criterion for all objects and coverings gives positive right-derived abelian evaluation vanishing. Evaluation at the terminal object computes global sections. Apply lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification to identify its rightDerived groups with the homology of derived global sections of the degree-zero single complex. Then lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison identifies these groups with Sheaf.H (Ext from the constant integer sheaf). This proves the subsingleton with abelian carriers in universe u+1 on X : Scheme.{u}.
